title: Accounts
chipIsolatedTip: Each account has its own config directory, so different sessions can use different accounts at once
chipHostActiveTip: This tool keeps its login on the machine, so only one account is in effect; changing the default account changes the machine's login
chipSharedIde: Shares its login with the IDE extension
autoFailoverTip: When a session hits a usage limit, move to the next usable account in list order
nativeLoggedInWho: {{tool}} on this machine is signed in as {{who}}
nativeNotLoggedIn: {{tool}} isn't signed in on this machine
nativeKeyMissing: {{tool}} on this machine is set to {{method}} but it isn't ready
envOverrideWarn: Environment variable {{env}} is set and may override the account settings
hostActiveHint: Changing the default account changes the {{tool}} login on this machine, including {{tool}} run directly in a terminal.
orderHint: Automatic switching picks accounts in this order; drag ⋮⋮ to reorder.
deleteConfirm: Delete account "{{label}}"? Its saved credentials are deleted too.
activateConfirm: {{count}} {{tool}} sessions are running. After the switch {{tool}} on this machine uses "{{label}}", and so do those sessions on their next request.
exportedToast: Credential bundle copied to the clipboard
optLoginClaudeSub: Authorize in a browser; on a remote host, paste back the code the page shows
optLoginCodexDeviceSub: Open a link and enter a code; works on remote hosts too
optLoginCodexBrowserSub: Finishes by itself after you authorize in this computer's browser
optLoginCursorSub: Authorize via a link, nothing to type
optLoginKiroSub: In-app sign-in supports Builder ID only
optKiroTerminalSub: Run kiro-cli login in a terminal, then come back and save it
optLoginQoderSub: Choose an account via a link, nothing to type
optCodebuddyTerminal: Sign in in a terminal, then save
optCodebuddyTerminalSub: CodeBuddy has no login command; sign in with /login in its own UI
optLoginAgySub: Authorize in a browser and paste back the code
optApiKeyClaudeSub: An Anthropic key or a compatible endpoint
optApiKeyCodexSub: An OpenAI key, or a provider in config.toml
optApiKeyCursorSub: Checked on save, which also reads the email and plan; doesn't touch this machine's login
optApiKeyAgySub: Each session can use a different key
optCaptureSub: Keep a copy of the {{tool}} account signed in on this machine
optCaptureCodexOauth: Save only this machine's ChatGPT login
optCaptureCodexOauthSub: This machine goes through provider "{{provider}}"; this saves just the login in ~/.codex/auth.json
optCursorEnvKeySub: This machine sets the variable; save it as an API key account
optImportSub: Paste or pick the JSON exported on another device
deviceIntro: Open the authorization page, sign in, then enter this code:
waitingBrowser: Waiting for you to finish in the browser…
expired: The code has expired; start again
linkIntro: Open the sign-in page in a browser and sign in; this finishes by itself.
linkRemoteHint: Works for remote hosts too: open the link in a browser on any device.
hostActiveLoginNote: Signing in doesn't touch the current {{tool}} login on this machine; the result is saved as a new account you can make the default later.
pasteStep1: Open the authorization page and sign in
pasteStep2: The page then shows a code (or lands on an address that doesn't load); copy it and paste it below
pasteLabel: Code or the address you landed on
pasteLocalHint: When you authorize on this computer it usually finishes by itself.
cliPrompt: The CLI is waiting for input:
namePlaceholderWait: Filled in once the email is read; you can also type one
terminalTitleCodebuddy: Sign in to CodeBuddy in a terminal
terminalTitleKiro: Sign in to Kiro in a terminal
terminalStep1: Open a terminal session (this switches to it; reopen Accounts afterwards)
terminalStep2Codebuddy: Run this command and type /login in its UI
terminalStep2Kiro: Run this command and choose Google, GitHub or your organization
terminalStep3: When you're signed in, come back and click "Save this machine's login"
terminalNotDetected: No {{tool}} login found on this machine yet
terminalSaved: This login is already saved as "{{label}}"
codebuddyIdeNote: The CodeBuddy IDE extension shares this login, so switching accounts switches the extension too.
kiroTerminalNote: Signing in in a terminal replaces the current Kiro login on this machine.
fieldAuthTokenHint: some relays use it instead of an API key
allowFailoverLabel: Can be switched to when other accounts run out of quota
cursorKeyHint: Saving checks the key and reads its email and plan. The key only lives in session processes and doesn't change this machine's Cursor login.
keyOnlyHint: {{tool}} reads only this variable; there's no base URL or model setting.
drawerFootHint: Running sessions use the new settings the next time their process starts
oauthEditHint: For login accounts only the name and automatic switching can change; sign in again to use another account.
importPlaceholder: Paste the JSON bundle exported on another device, or read it from a file…
exportWarn: It contains login credentials; keep it safe
actualProviderLine: Codex actually uses provider "{{provider}}" from config.toml: {{url}}
actualProviderLineNoUrl: Codex actually uses provider "{{provider}}" from config.toml
actualKeyFromEnv: The API key comes from environment variable {{env}}
actualKeyMissing: Environment variable {{env}} isn't set, so Codex has no API key and requests will fail
actualOpenaiAuthLine: Requests carry the login from ~/.codex/auth.json to this provider
actualOauthUnused: ~/.codex/auth.json has a ChatGPT login, but it isn't being used
savedAsOauth: This account is saved as an OAuth account
codexMismatchWarn: This account is saved as a ChatGPT login ({{email}}), but its config.toml selects provider "{{provider}}": requests go to that provider without this login, and the quota has nothing to do with this plan.
convertToApiKeyConfirm: Convert "{{label}}" to an API key account for provider {{provider}}: the current value of {{env}} is saved as its key and it keeps using that provider. The ChatGPT login is backed up so you can switch back.
convertToOauthConfirm: Stop "{{label}}" using provider {{provider}}: model_provider is removed from its config.toml, and sessions started afterwards use the ChatGPT login and that plan's quota.
